- **Tool names:** each of the 5 task tools appears only in its own hub. The scripted scan found no `card_ext_*` / `card_agg_*` ids and no "first call / checklist / roadmap / see the / refer to / described in / set out elsewhere / unless otherwise / adjustments may / certain customers" phrasing. The only "then call" hits are the own-tool invocation blocks.

- **Titles:** "Credit Line Review Desk Note", "Billing Error Desk Note: Foreign Purchases Posted Twice", "Credit Memo Standard: New Credit Line at a Line Review" and the factor titles all name general subjects or the on_request policy's own request type. None mirrors the task ("credit limit for furniture", "Casa Lusitana", etc.).
- **Baseline hinting:**
  - The worksheet's "In this worksheet the related interest base is taken as zero, the interest-bearing balance as the latest statement balance and the billing-time fraction as one" (and "the accrual days are taken as zero", "the related other charge is taken as zero") carries the source baseline's own "as standard … is zero / is one" defaults.
  - Line review: the baseline states "0.5 times" with no hint.
  - This is the source's baseline form, not a rendering addition, so it is not RED. Policy-side note: a baseline that names its own variable quantities at a standard value does let a reader infer they can vary. That is inherent to the source design.
- **Factor docs:** none names or points at the computation document or another factor; none says which tier customers fall on; none writes task evidence.
  - The Finch Circle docs' hypothetical rows "(Diamond is not a Silver or Gold tier)" / "(Platinum is not a Silver or Gold tier)" clarify a ladder boundary on hypothetical members, not a named mistake. Judged not RED.
- **Findability:** each depended-on or factor doc is reachable by record words ("foreign transaction fee", "posted twice", "duplicate charge", "Finch Circle", "late fee", "returned payment fee", "promotional balance", "last credit line change"), not only by phrasing borrowed from the dependent doc.
